clue.text: Pay attention: the 12th letter is X

parts.note: L is the twelfth letter of the alphabet
taken as written
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A teacher demands attention while spelling out which letter is X in some code.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes the rest look like a statement to be heard; in fact it spells the answer piece by piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen is to give heed, an everyday synonym for paying attention.

clue.text: Intriguing calls from Member of Parliament in support of old people

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits below the one it holds up

parts.note: the Inca were the ancient people of Peru
a parliament is the collective noun for owls, so its member is an owl, whose calls are hoots

explanation.surface: Someone is plotting, with a politician's appeals backing pensioners.
explanation.walkthrough: Member of Parliament looks like an MP, but parliament here is the collective noun for owls.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in cahoots means conspiring together, so intriguing in the sense of plotting secretly.

clue.text: Toy gun used to hold up Tesco, primarily

indicators.note: in a down answer the lower piece holds up the one above it, so the gun goes beneath
primarily asks for the first letter of the following word

parts.note: Tesco is a British supermarket chain
a rifle is a kind of gun

explanation.surface: A toy gun was used to rob a Tesco supermarket.
explanation.walkthrough: Hold up suggests a robbery; here the gun is simply under the letter in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle with something is to toy with it, treating it without seriousness.

clue.text: German drilling near built-up area — this goes on late

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: the letter for German bores into the town, sitting inside it

parts.note: a town is a built-up area

explanation.surface: A German company is drilling close to a town, work that goes on late into the night.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cryptic phrase at the end: a garment put on late at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightgown is a garment worn in bed, so it is put on at a late hour.

clue.text: Does this protect pig's head? I don't care!

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
a hat is what covers and protects the head

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a pig needs a helmet and gets a shrug in reply.
explanation.definitionFit: So what? is a dismissive retort expressing indifference, the same as saying one does not mind.

clue.text: Where I saw mouse and rat is demolished

indicators.note: demolished tells us the letters are knocked down and rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone reports vermin sightings in a building being torn down.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'is' does double duty in the surface but is part of the fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouse might be spotted on a step of a staircase, so the location is a fair cryptic definition.

clue.text: Said Reading inmate once stole king's game

indicators.note: said signals that the writer's surname is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: Oscar Wilde was imprisoned in Reading Gaol
a boa is a long scarf or stole
R stands for rex, king

explanation.surface: A former prisoner of Reading is accused of stealing the king's quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: Stole looks like a verb but is the scarf. Reading is the English town with the gaol, not the activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild boar is hunted as quarry and served as meat, so it counts as game.

clue.text: Put out a football team with no wingers?

indicators.note: the players on the wings are removed, so the end letters go

parts.note: Rangers is a Glasgow football club

explanation.surface: A manager fielding a side without wide players would be upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To anger someone is to annoy them, and put out means annoyed or irritated.

clue.text: Attractive female avoided making an impression

indicators.note: the letter for female is avoided, so it is left out of the word

parts.note: fetching means attractive

explanation.surface: An attractive woman kept out of sight while a crowd sought to impress.
explanation.definitionFit: Etching is the process of incising a design into a plate to make a print, an impression.

clue.text: Exercising caution with deal could be enlightening

indicators.note: exercising suggests putting the letters through their paces, working them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being careful with a business deal may teach you something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something educational is instructive, imparting knowledge, which is what enlightening means.

clue.text: Perfect self-image inspiring Mahler's last movement

parts.note: all in the sense of complete, entire

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the self-image takes the letter inside it

parts.note: ego is one's sense of self

indicators.note: last asks for the closing letter of the name before it, the composer's

parts.note: the final letter of the composer's surname

explanation.surface: A composer's flawless view of himself inspired his final symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: Movement is the musical sense: a section of a symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is a tempo marking that names a lively section of a symphony or sonata.

clue.text: Old book well-read son renders illegible

parts.note: a literate person is well-read

explanation.surface: An old book, a learned son, and text that becomes impossible to read.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate writing is to wipe it out so that it can no longer be read.

clue.text: Stuff something warming from Vietnam inside coat

indicators.note: inside places the soup within the coat

parts.note: an ulster is a long loose overcoat
pho is a hot Vietnamese noodle soup

explanation.surface: Someone tucks a hand warmer from Vietnam inside a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: To upholster is to pad furniture with stuffing and cover it with fabric.

clue.text: Live tracks — what's essential to Rolling Stone?

parts.note: be means to exist, to live
RY is short for railway, a set of tracks

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its very centre, so the middle letter is taken

parts.note: the single central letter of the seven-letter word

explanation.surface: A live recording by the Rolling Stones prompts the question of what drives the band.
explanation.walkthrough: Rolling Stone reads as the band; the stone is the definition and Rolling just supplies its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Beryl is a mineral gemstone, of which emerald and aquamarine are varieties.

clue.text: Tiny part or larger part of anatomy

indicators.note: the answer takes up more than half the letters of the word, so it is its larger part

parts.note: four consecutive letters inside the seven-letter word

explanation.surface: A contrast between a minute and a sizeable part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the smallest particle of an element, a minute constituent.

clue.text: Where to buy feathers cheap?

parts.note: down is the soft fine feathers of a bird
a market is where goods are bought

explanation.surface: A shopper asks where to find cheap feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Downmarket describes goods aimed at the lower, less expensive end of the trade.

clue.text: Disreputable hunter mostly spearing other people

indicators.note: the hunter is driven through the other people like a spear, sitting inside them

parts.note: other people are not us

indicators.note: mostly drops the final letter

parts.note: Orion is the hunter of Greek myth and the constellation

explanation.surface: A shady hunter is impaling bystanders.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means famous for something bad, so having a poor reputation.

clue.text: Clever clogs translated Low Latin term for Greek crowns

indicators.note: in a down answer the crowning piece sits on top
a term is an end, so the term for a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word Greek

indicators.note: translated suggests the words are turned into another form, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone renders a Low Latin word for Greek crowns, showing off their learning.
explanation.walkthrough: Low Latin is a real term for medieval Latin, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever clogs is a British jibe for a smart alec, a person who acts as though they know everything.

clue.text: Most fly south a month before trial

parts.note: MAR is the calendar abbreviation for March
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: Birds fly south a month before some trial run.
explanation.walkthrough: Fly is an adjective here, an informal word for sharp or knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly in slang means sharp and clever, so the most fly is the cleverest.

clue.text: Native potting house plant

indicators.note: potting puts something into a pot, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: innate means native, inborn
a semi is a semi-detached house

explanation.surface: A gardener is potting a native houseplant.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant is the verb: to implant seed.
explanation.definitionFit: To inseminate is to introduce semen, to sow or implant seed.

clue.text: Cocktail you are delivered by standing order

parts.note: SO is the banking abbreviation for a standing order

indicators.note: delivered means spoken, so the words you are are heard as two letters

parts.note: UR is text-speak for you are

explanation.surface: Drinks are delivered to you on a regular order.
explanation.definitionFit: A sour is a mixed drink made with spirit, lemon juice and sugar, such as a whisky sour.

clue.text: Set aside last of meat from bone for regional dish

indicators.note: set aside means removed, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: the patella is the kneecap bone

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter of meat

explanation.surface: A cook strips meat from the bone to make a local dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a rice dish from the Valencia region of Spain.

clue.text: Regressive playwright striking woman's bottom

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the remaining letters are read in reverse
striking out means deleting, so the woman is struck from the name

parts.note: Richard Brinsley Sheridan wrote The Rivals and The School for Scandal
she is a woman

explanation.surface: A backward-looking dramatist hits a woman on her behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Striking looks violent but means deleting; bottom is the lowest point, not the anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, its very bottom.

clue.text: Dog in uproar? Beat it!

parts.note: a din is a loud noise
beat it means go away

explanation.surface: A dog causes a racket and is told to clear off.
explanation.definitionFit: The dingo is the wild dog of Australia.

clue.text: Medicine dealer's file on girl's case of bilharzia

parts.note: her is the possessive for a girl

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the disease name
a list is a file of items

explanation.surface: A pharmacist holds a file on a girl's tropical infection.
explanation.walkthrough: Bilharzia is a parasitic disease; only its first and last letters are wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbalist prescribes and sells remedies made from plants, so deals in medicine.

clue.text: Practical clothing for horseplay

wordplay.note: the clothing of a word is its outside letters; spoken as two letters with a conjunction between them

explanation.surface: Sensible wear for rough play.
explanation.walkthrough: The clothing of a word is its outer letters: the first and last of horseplay, joined by and, spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Handy means useful and convenient, a near synonym of practical.

clue.text: Largely against boarding train without a torch

indicators.note: boarding means getting on board, so the shortened word goes inside
without removes the letter a

parts.note: to learn is to be trained
taken as written

indicators.note: largely keeps most of the word, losing the last letter

parts.note: anti means against

explanation.surface: Someone, against regulations, gets on a train without a flashlight.
explanation.walkthrough: Train is the verb here, not the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp, which in British English a torch also is.

clue.text: Distribute coal in small dispensers

indicators.note: distributing scatters the letters, which are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Coal is handed out in little lots.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilcans are containers with spouts for dispensing lubricating oil.

clue.text: Left newlywed's belly needing larger dress size?

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
the belly is the middle of the body, so the two central letters of newlywed

explanation.surface: A newlywed's expanding waistline after the honeymoon means bigger clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Portly means stout and rotund, so a portly person may need clothes in bigger sizes.

clue.text: Most skilful when cycling, unlikely to fall over

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: ablest means most able, most skilful

explanation.surface: The best riders stay upright on a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stable is steady and firmly balanced, so it will not topple.
